A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoCa-BO research. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, figures, equations and complete appendices despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original SCM simulations comparing CoCa-BO with CaBO and CoBO, including high-dimensional and noise experiments in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V3 retains these original simulations and adds BO-backend and context-removal experiments in Appendix A.5 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: V2 Algorithm 2 uses reward-updated MAB-UCB for scope selection. V3 Sections 3 and B.1 instead specify selection using the running average of historical GP-UCB values plus an exploration margin, with Algorithm 2 formalizing this procedure. This changes a central selection component while retaining the contextual BO framework.

E1.justification: The synthetic PSA environments, toy causal configurations, high-dimensional environment and noise scenarios are retained. The new backend and context-removal ablations reuse the environment from v2 Appendix C.1, now v3 Appendix A.2; they do not introduce another dataset or task.

E2.justification: CaBO and CoBO remain the comparators in the retained benchmark experiments. V3 Figure 7 adds evaluated CoCa-BO variants using BoTorch and GPflow alongside HEBO, plus a variant without contextual inputs.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces controls that vary the BO backend or remove context while preserving the intervention variables and hierarchical design. Section 6 also reverses the printed instantaneous-regret formula from observed reward minus optimal expectation to optimal expectation minus observed reward. The 700-iteration budget remains unchanged; these edits do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct component ablations absent from v2: backend substitution tests whether convergence depends on HEBO, and context removal isolates the contribution of contextual information while preserving the hierarchical method. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence beyond the retained noise and dimensionality analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 110 random seeds and a general convention of 1.96 standard-error bars. V2 Figure 5 additionally identifies its noise-study shading as one standard deviation; v3 retains that plot but removes this specification. This reduces uncertainty-reporting detail without establishing any change in runs or plotted bands.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, high-dimensional and noise plots retain the same results after relocation and renumbering. V3 Figure 7 adds findings that all three BO backends converge, with HEBO slightly better, and that removing context produces a suboptimal plateau. These are additional controlled comparisons, not performance gains over v2 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: V2 Theorem 4.1 and Appendix A analyze noncontextual multi-function BO to obtain a CaBO bound. V3 Theorem 1 and Appendix B introduce context-averaged regret, contextual assumptions, worst-case and instance-dependent bounds, and new concentration and selection lemmas. Appendix C adds information-gain sum bounds and an optimal-arm uniqueness analysis.

C1.justification: V2's central theoretical contribution is a probabilistic CaBO regret bound, with empirical support for the contextual extension. V3's abstract, contribution list and conclusion claim worst-case and instance-dependent high-probability guarantees for CoCa-BO itself under GP assumptions. This materially expands the scope of the principal theoretical claim.

C2.justification: V2 Section 6.3 claims maintained convergence even at noise standard deviation 6.25. V3 Section 6 instead says convergence is unclear there and supported up to 1.25. V3 also explains when suboptimality gaps permit improved regret scaling and interprets the context ablation as isolating missing context as the cause of suboptimality.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix A.5 documents the alternative backends, their GPyTorch or TensorFlow dependencies, and how context is removed. Conversely, v2's explicit statement that HEBO uses default parameters is omitted. Hardware requirements and the general Pyro implementation disclosure remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning through discussions of Functional Causal BO, Model-Based Causal BO, additional causal-bandit research and multitask GPs. Section 5 contrasts implementation requirements, confounding assumptions, regret scaling and information sharing, extending well beyond v2's comparisons with CaBO, CoBO and discrete mixed-policy learning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, background precedes the proposed algorithm, and related work moves after the theoretical section. Previously separate experimental appendices are consolidated before the expanded proofs. New notation explanations, an appendix contents page and author information changes further revise the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: V3 changes the main text from two columns to one, adds an algorithm-overview diagram, a two-panel ablation figure, and acronym, notation and information-gain tables. It redraws the introductory causal graph and moves the noise plot into the main text. Existing empirical plots are reused rather than replaced with new results.

improvement.justification: V3 adds informative ablations and a more cautious interpretation of extreme-noise behavior. However, its central expansion beyond v2—the contextual regret guarantee—contains an unresolved proof step. Appendix B.2, page 27, bounds action loss by the range of optimal rewards across contexts, defined in Lemma 3. That range can be zero while action loss is positive, so it does not justify the stated inequality. The empirical and explanatory gains coexist with uncertainty in the new central theoretical claim, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment.
